MANAGED MERCHANT FLEET / FIRST SETUP

Prepare your merchant fleet.

Register the merchants you want to run together. Review their source packages, public hosts and fixed slots, then download a setup packet for the original fleet operator.

Fleet launch workbenchRETAINED NATIVE SETUP

Complete these items.

    Choose the host directories and listeners.

    Use the paths and ports on your Linux merchant host. Setup creates a distinct original release store for every merchant slot and retains the completed plan in the private fleet directory.

    The downloaded packet contains the editable declaration and native launch instructions.

    Start with an absent or empty directory. Use this same retained directory when resuming setup or changing interfaces.

    Choose a new directory whose parent exists on the host. Its MCP configuration will open the same private fleet and published plan.

    A separate loopback port for the original managed fleet workspace. Use 0 for automatic allocation.

    Fixed fleet ports and slots

    The original gateway routes each configured public host to its selected merchant.

    The private control listener used by the original operator.

    Each merchant receives the next group of consecutive slot ports. Review shows the exact allocation.

    Use two to four distinct names. The first slot receives each merchant’s initial release.

    Choose distinct ingress, control, workspace and merchant ports. Native setup reserves its declared fleet ports while preparing the stores. The original operator acquires the running listeners when you open the fleet.

    Register each merchant and its source packages.

    Choose the actual public host declared by each prepared source. Register package aliases for the original operator, then choose the package and release ID that should serve first.

    MERCHANTS

    Declare two to thirty-two merchants. Every merchant keeps its own hosts, package aliases and release stores.

    Enter source paths as they will exist on the merchant host. Relative package paths resolve from the saved setup declaration. Native setup validates each original source and its configured HTTPS origin before selecting its release.

    Review the fleet and download its launch packet.

    Review the exact merchant hosts, startup packages, slot stores and listener ports. The local setup command passes the declaration through the original source and release APIs before publishing the fleet plan.

    Keep the editable draft with the setup declaration for the next host session.

    ONE RETAINED FLEET · TERMINAL, BROWSER AND MCP

    Keep the fleet intact between sessions.

    Resume the same setup

    Repeat the same setup command after an interruption. The original retained stores identify completed staging and selection, and setup continues from that progress.

    Open the original operator

    Use the published plan and private fleet directory in the terminal, browser workspace or merchant MCP. Close the current foreground owner before opening another interface.

    Review later releases

    Register the next package, stage it in an available slot, and use the original review and activation flow. The fleet retains its release mapping, drain state and rollback history.
